prize_parts.citation: for the development of orthogonal translation systems that expand the genetic code and allow site-specific incorporation of noncanonical amino acids into proteins in living cells

statement.case_for: After the full round-1 exchange I keep B054 as my preferred single-part prize. Its scientific case is finished: the orthogonal tRNA/synthetase concept was made to work in living cells by Schultz and Wang, and Chin generalised it to multiple codons, orthogonal ribosomes and multicellular animals. Two decades of independent use, including as site-specific spectroscopic probes and mechanistic substitutions in enzymes of the kind I study, show that the interpretation is stable. The credit divides into founding concept and first demonstration, then extension to whole organisms and recoded genomes, which fits the three-name cap. The chair asks whether an approved degrader should be a precondition. I do not set that as a rule, but B057 asks the committee to settle a contested third name and a two-lineage citation while the clinical picture is still moving. B054 asks it to settle neither. Five members name B054 as an alternative and none has argued against it on scientific grounds, so it is the configuration with the least open disagreement.
statement.case_against: The reservations are real. Mehl and Yokoyama are excluded by the cap, and the field lacked a single decisive moment, so the citation must be written carefully to reflect the Schultz, Wang and Chin lineage. It follows the biomolecular-tool prizes of 2018, 2020 and 2024, and a committee could judge that one more such prize is repetitive. The strongest objection is that B057 is the more novel mode of action: five members put it first with an identical laureate set, and its mechanism (ternary complexes, E3 recruitment, cereblon as the thalidomide target) is confirmed. If the committee is willing to award before any approval, its case on originality is stronger than mine, and I would not obstruct it.

responses.point: Aqvist moved from B037 to B057 and now prefers Handa to Ciulli as third name, because cereblon changed the mechanistic understanding of existing drugs while the VHL work was a later structural and design advance. He also says waiting would not change the credit picture.
responses.response: Part of this persuades me. Cereblon is a discovery about what existing drugs do, and a citation that leaves glues without a founder would be thin. I also accept that waiting is not obviously the way to resolve who deserves credit. Where I still differ is on whether the picture is settled. Ciulli's contribution is more than a refinement: the VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures turned PROTAC design into a rational chemical problem, and the Crews, Deshaies and Handa trio leaves out that structural basis, as well as Sakamoto's role in the first PROTAC. I now think Handa is the better third name than Ciulli if B057 is chosen, because the glue strand has approved drugs behind it, but I do not think the omissions are small.

responses.point: Chabes keeps Crews, Deshaies and Handa because the trio spans concept and mechanism, and says he would accept B054 as the preferred prize if the committee finds B057 premature.
responses.response: I take that as the most constructive statement on the table. I accept that Handa is the stronger third name for a prize built around induced proximity, and I withdraw my suggestion that Ciulli should displace him. My remaining objection is to the combination: PROTACs and glues are presented as one achievement, but the three people honoured come from two quite different histories. If B057 goes forward I would want the citation to say explicitly that cereblon is credited as the mechanism behind glue degraders and thalidomide-type drugs, not as part of the PROTAC design story. If B057 does not reach five votes, I would ask Chabes and the others who listed B054 as a fallback to say whether they would vote for it as a final configuration, not only keep it as an alternative.

responses.point: Somfai argues that B068 has three decades of confirmed use and a clean two-person attribution, that the 2010 prize recognised C-C bond formation, and that Kosugi's tin-amide coupling was stoichiometric and narrow, so credit rightly goes to Buchwald and Hartwig.
responses.response: The Kosugi argument is convincing. A general catalytic, ligand-controlled method is different from a stoichiometric tin reagent, and I no longer see priority as an obstacle. On the 2010 point, I accept that C-N bond formation needed its own ligand design and mechanism, which is a stronger distinction than I granted in round 1. My remaining hesitation is one of degree: the committee would be honouring a second member of a family it has already recognised, while B054 and B057 each give a new capability. That is a judgement about relative novelty and not about quality, and it is why I now name B068 as a serious alternative, behind B057, in case B054 does not carry.

responses.point: Linke, as chair, would take Ciulli over Deshaies if the prize centred on bifunctional degraders, opposes splitting B057 into two prizes, and notes that the committee has not traditionally required an approved drug when mechanism and generality are confirmed.
responses.response: I agree that a two-part split would spend the whole prize on a single area, and I accept your point that an approved drug has not been a formal requirement. That is why I do not call B057 disqualified by timing. My view is only that, when two candidates are both excellent, I prefer the one whose credit the committee can write down today without a contested cut. I would not replace Deshaies with Ciulli, since Deshaies's demonstration of the PROTAC principle in cells is part of the founding concept, and I would keep the split between one-part and two-part prizes out of this decision.

responses.point: Zou prefers B068 because it asks the committee to settle neither allocation nor timing questions, and says she would support B057 if the clinical evidence is judged sufficient.
responses.response: I agree with the principle behind her choice: a configuration should be judged partly by how many open questions it asks the committee to resolve. By that test B054 and B068 are close, and the difference between us is the weight given to novelty within the prize record, since B054 adds a new capability for placing chemically defined groups in proteins in living cells. I accept her wording for a B068 citation (catalytic, ligand-controlled, general) and I would not oppose it if B054 falls short.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will award B057 before any degrader is approved, and whether the Crews, Deshaies and Handa cut would hold once the omissions of Ciulli and Sakamoto are discussed in full.
Whether a three-name cap that excludes Mehl and Yokoyama will be accepted for B054, and whether the citation can credit the Schultz, Wang and Chin lineage without implying others did not contribute.
Whether another biomolecular-tool prize after 2018, 2020 and 2024 will be seen as repetitive, and whether I weight that concern too little.
Whether my preference for the most settled configuration undervalues the novelty of induced-proximity pharmacology, which most colleagues weight more heavily.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. I am a Stockholm University colleague of Xiaodong Zou, who is a committee member and not a candidate, so no recusal issue arises. My research on respiratory enzymes could use genetic-code-expansion tools (B054), but I have no documented collaboration, funding link or other tie to Schultz, Chin or Wang or to any other credited name on the shortlist, and I do not request recusal.
